Subject: POC trial planning — workload & success criteria (Acme Health)

Alex / Priya — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment ahead of the POC kickoff.

Summary of what we discussed (high level):
- Goal: 3-week POC to validate latency, throughput, and accuracy for Acme’s summary/triage workflow.
- Primary success criteria (draft): p50 latency < 200ms; p90 < 500ms under steady-state load, throughput to support 120 RPS steady with ability to handle bursts up to ~400 RPS for short windows; model quality to meet the evaluation set baseline (we'll formalize metrics).
- Key integrations: API-based traffic to Redwood hosted endpoint, sample dataset for blind evaluation, SSO for the team, and a shared test account for instrumentation.

Immediate asks for trial planning (can you confirm these items?):
1) Workload profile: steady RPS, typical/peak token lengths (prompt vs. response), expected concurrency, and typical burst patterns (duration/frequency).
2) Test dataset: sample of ~2-5k requests or a representative subset; transfer method (Drive link or S3).
3) Ownership: who on Acme will be the integration/infra owner and who is the evaluation owner?
4) Any procurement timelines or SOW gating items we should be aware of.

Proposed POC timeline (we can adjust):
- Week 0 (onboarding): account setup, API keys, runbook review, baseline smoke tests.
- Week 1: baseline traffic at steady RPS, baseline quality evaluation.
- Week 2: scale tests, burst/latency validation, run cost/perf analysis.
- End: handoff meeting with results + decision rubric.

Proposed ownership (Redwood): Ben (lead for onboarding & account setup), Marissa (lead for evaluation & success criteria), Dylan (infra & perf tuning). Please tell us if you'd like different owners.

I've attached our POC runbook template (poc_runbook.xlsx) to this thread — please populate the workload and dataset fields and return when convenient. If it helps, a few example values that would let us size the trial quickly:
- steady RPS: 100-140
- burst RPS (typical business spikes): 300-420 for 2-5 minutes
- avg prompt token length: ~60-80 tokens
- avg response token length: ~200-300 tokens
- concurrency (simultaneous unique callers): 8-16

Next steps (short):
- Alex/Priya: share the workload profile CSV and one sample evaluation file by EOD Wed 4/4.
- Redwood: send our draft runbook + proposed onboarding calendar by EOD Tue 4/3.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this scheduled.
—
Ben Carter

Alex — this is great, thanks for the CSV and Drive link. A few follow-ups and a proposed config for the trial based on your profile:

1) Config suggestion
- Initial: hosted Redwood endpoint with a medium reserved concurrency pool to match steady RPS; auto-burst policy to cover the 3-5 minute spikes.
- Model & perf: we’ll start with redwood-inference-v3 (default quantized profile) to balance cost & latency; can swap to a higher-capacity variant if quality/latency needs it.
- Instrumentation: we’ll enable prefixKV caching for repeated prompts and continuous batching to smooth tails.

2) Proposed (measurable) success criteria
- Performance: p50 latency < 250ms and p90 < 600ms during steady-state (100-130 RPS). During burst windows (350-420 RPS), p90 should stay under 1.2s with no more than 2% error rate.
- Quality: on the provided evaluation set, automated metrics (F1/ROUGE where applicable) must not regress >5% relative to your internal baseline; Priya will confirm the target thresholds.
- Reliability: zero data-loss incidents, and end-to-end requests successfully processed for 99.5% of calls over the 3-week period.

3) Runbook items we need you to fill (we'll annotate):
- traffic routing endpoint(s) and auth method (API key vs OAuth)
- sample failed-request logs if available
- a short list of production-like prompts to use for QA

4) Owners & timeline
- Ben (Redwood) for onboarding & runbook updates
- Marissa (Redwood) for evaluation and metric collection
- Dylan (Redwood) for perf tuning; Alex (Acme) for infra exec and Priya (Acme) for product sign-off

We will prepare the onboarding calendar (proposed dates below) and the initial test harness by EOD today so you can review. Also attaching the populated POC runbook (poc_runbook.xlsx) with our annotations.

If that sounds good, next will be: Redwood creates test account + API key, schedule onboarding call (30-45m), and begin baseline tests.


Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
